I  /  Counting the fleet

When does a car
count as active?

Counting the fleet03

Count each vehicle once per active year

1,926,507raw transactions
1,909,074eligible transactions
1,349,135vehicle-years
397,023distinct eligible vehicles

Which cars qualify?

Keep road-going plug-ins with a Washington county and a use class subject to renewal. Remove duplicate rows.

Which row counts?

One vehicle ID counts once per active year. Use title records to identify new entrants. The last record of the year assigns the county.

Two missing years define an exit

Bridge a single missing year only when a record appears on both sides. A later record after a two-year gap counts as a return.

II  /  Growth and geography

Where did the
fleet grow?

Growth and geography06

Washington’s plug-in fleet grew fivefold

79.8%

of active plug-ins were battery electric in 2025.

Their share rose from 69.2% in 2019. Over the same six years, the fleet’s mean age rose from 2.58 to 3.05 years.

Growth and geography07

King County’s share fell as its fleet grew

55.1% → 49.7%

King’s share of Washington’s plug-ins, 2019–2025

King’s count rose from 29,067 to 134,145. By 2025 it still had more than twice as many plug-ins per resident as the rest of the state.

Growth and geography08

Starting size explained little of county growth

9%

of variation in county log growth was explained by starting stock.

Across 39 counties, the correlation was −0.31. Small starting counts made some growth multiples especially sensitive to a handful of cars.

III  /  Measuring variation

How much
variation should
we expect?

Measuring variation10

Weekly arrivals varied more than Poisson predicted

873

weeks of new-vehicle entries

A negative binomial model allows extra variation. Its nominal 95% band covered about 95% of observed weeks.

Measuring variation11

Larger samples gave steadier estimates of age

3.05

years was the mean age of the 2025 fleet.

Individual ages were right-skewed. With 500 vehicles per sample, the standard deviation of the sample mean was just 0.133 years.

IV  /  Leaving the records

Can we tell which
cars will leave?

Leaving the records13

Recent cohorts had similar exit rates by powertrain

7.39%

age-adjusted exit probability for a battery electric in the 2021 cohort.

Plug-in hybrids were at 7.62%. The age-adjusted odds ratio was 1.03, with a 95% confidence interval spanning equal odds.

Leaving the records14

Vehicle histories only weakly ranked future exits

7.59%

mean predicted exit probability in the 2023 test cohort.

The observed rate was 7.53%. The fleet average was close even though the model struggled to identify which cars would leave.
